original_question: Determine the exact bounded compact approximation constant M(H^p) for every 1 <= p < infinity, and determine the exact dual compact approximation constant M*(H^p) for every 1 < p < infinity, where M(H^p) is the greatest lower bound of the constants M for which every finite subset of H^p can be approximated pointwise by a compact operator T with ||I - T|| <= M, and M*(H^p) is the analogous greatest lower bound defined through approximation of finite subsets of the dual space by adjoints of compact operators.
target_in_paper: Section 5.3, Open problem 5.5 on the exact values of M(H^p) for 1 ≤ p < ∞ and M*(H^p) for 1 < p < ∞.
correct_elements: Your draft points to the right open problem and gets the main parameter ranges right: the paper asks for the exact value of M(H^p) for 1 ≤ p < ∞ and for the exact value of M*(H^p) for 1 < p < ∞. It also correctly treats M(H^p) and M*(H^p) as BCAP/DCAP constants defined through approximation of finite sets by compact operators and their adjoints.
missing_details: Specify that H^p means the classical complex Hardy space H^p(𝕋) on the unit circle 𝕋, not a weighted Hardy space H^p(w) or a general abstract Hardy space H[X(w)].
Add the missing quantifier 'for every ε > 0' in both definitions; the BCAP/DCAP constants are defined by approximation of finite sets to arbitrary prescribed accuracy ε.

Replace the phrase 'approximated pointwise' by the paper-faithful formulation 'approximated in norm on each element of a finite subset'; the approximation is in the Banach-space norm, not pointwise on 𝕋.
Make explicit that T ranges over compact linear operators T ∈ K(H^p), and that the norm control is ||I_{H^p} - T|| ≤ M.
In the dual formulation, state explicitly that one uses the adjoint T* of the same compact operator T on H^p, acting on finite subsets of (H^p)*, with ||φ - T*φ||_(H^p)* < ε.
If the question is to be fully stand-alone, include the ambient complex-function setting used in the paper: measurable complex-valued functions on 𝕋 with normalized Lebesgue measure.
refined_question: For the classical complex Hardy spaces H^p = H^p(𝕋) on the unit circle 𝕋, determine the exact value of the bounded compact approximation constant M(H^p) for every 1 ≤ p < ∞ and the exact value of the dual compact approximation constant M*(H^p) for every 1 < p < ∞, where M(H^p) is the greatest lower bound of the constants M > 0 such that for every ε > 0 and every finite set F ⊂ H^p there exists a compact operator T ∈ K(H^p) with ||I_{H^p} - T|| ≤ M and ||f - Tf||_{H^p} < ε for all f ∈ F, and M*(H^p) is the greatest lower bound of the constants M > 0 such that for every ε > 0 and every finite set G ⊂ (H^p)* there exists a compact operator T ∈ K(H^p) with ||I_{H^p} - T|| ≤ M and ||φ - T*φ||_(H^p)* < ε for all φ ∈ G.
justification: This is exactly the paper's Open problem 5.5 in Section 5.3. Section 1 defines BCAP, DCAP, and the constants M(X), M*(X) through (1.3) and (1.4), and it introduces H^p as the classical Hardy-space notation for H[L^p]. The discussion leading into Open problem 5.5 says that the known information for classical Hardy spaces is the bound M(H^1) ≤ 2 obtained by specializing Theorem 1.3(a) to X = L^1 and w = 1, together with the bounds M(H^p), M*(H^p) ≤ 2^{|1-2/p|} from Theorem 1.2, and then asks for the exact values. So your draft is already very close to the paper's intent; the main things needed to make it fully stand-alone and paper-faithful are the ambient Hardy-space notation H^p(𝕋), the ε-quantifiers, and the precise dual formulation via T* on finite subsets of (H^p)*.
